title: Rust: Simple Compiler (Bytecode)
description: Build a compiler that generates bytecode from AST and run it on a VM.

steps.title: Define Bytecode Instructions
steps.description: Define an `Opcode` enum: `Push(f64)`, `Add`, `Sub`, `Mul`, `Div`, `Pop`, `Print`, `Halt`. Create a `Chunk` that stores a sequence of opcodes. Print the disassembly.
hints: `#[derive(Debug)] enum Opcode { Push(f64), Add, Sub, Mul, Div, Pop, Print, Halt }`

verification.failureMessage: Create and print a chunk with Push(42), Print, Halt.

steps.title: Stack-Based VM
steps.description: Implement a `VM` struct with a `value_stack: Vec<f64>`. Implement `run(&mut self, chunk: &Chunk)` that interprets opcodes. Test with `Push(2), Push(3), Add, Print, Halt` (should print 5).

verification.failureMessage: Run Push(2), Push(3), Add, Print and output 5.

steps.title: Compiler: Expression to Bytecode
steps.description: Write a compiler that takes an AST from your parser and generates bytecode. Compile `2 + 3 * 4` to bytecode and run it on the VM. Result should be 14.
hints: Walk the AST tree in postfix order.
BinaryOp: compile left, compile right, emit the operator opcode.
`2 + 3 * 4` → Push(2), Push(3), Push(4), Mul, Add, Print, Halt

steps.title: Variables and Environment
steps.description: Add `StoreVar(String)` and `LoadVar(String)` opcodes. Add a `variables: HashMap<String, f64>` to the VM. Compile `let x = 42; print x` with bytecode and run.
hints: StoreVar pops value from stack and stores in VM's variables.
LoadVar pushes the variable value onto the stack.
`let x = 42; print x` → Push(42), StoreVar("x"), LoadVar("x"), Print, Halt

verification.failureMessage: Compile and run 'let x = 42; print x' to get 42.

steps.title: Full Pipeline
steps.description: Create a full pipeline: source code → Lexer → Parser → Compiler → VM → output. Test with a multi-line program: `let x = 10; let y = 20; print x + y`. Print the compiled bytecode and the execution result.
hints: `let ast = Parser::new(tokens).parse(); let code = Compiler::new().compile(&ast); VM::new().run(&code);`
Print both bytecode disassembly and execution output.

verification.failureMessage: Compile 'let x=10; let y=20; print x+y' and print 30.
